title: Bitrig Now Builds CarPlay Apps
summary: Get started without an entitlement or paid Apple Developer account. Build on the go with Bitrig Remote, and try your changes on the drive home.
body_markdown:
For close to a decade I’ve had an idea for a CarPlay app. But I procrastinated building it because I didn’t know much about the CarPlay SDK, and what I did know was different enough to scare me off.


This weekend I finally built it. During my kids’ 30-minute swim lesson, from my iPhone. Then I used it on the drive home. It was glorious.


I could do it because:


**Bitrig can now build CarPlay apps and test them in its built-in simulator.**


Running your CarPlay app in a real car requires an entitlement from Apple and a paid Apple Developer account. So does testing it in[Xcode’s CarPlay Simulator](https://developer.apple.com/download/files/CarPlay-Developer-Guide.pdf) . But Bitrig lets you test your CarPlay app without either.


Here’s how it works:


-


**Build with CarPlay templates.** Bitrig knows every CarPlay category and which templates each one allows. It adds CarPlay to your existing iPhone app, following Apple’s[Human Interface Guidelines for CarPlay](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/carplay) .


-


**Run it in the CarPlay simulator.** Switch between your iPhone and its CarPlay screen using the device menu. Both your Mac and Bitrig Remote can show either screen.


-


**Test and refine it.** The agent taps through your CarPlay interface to test it with[Simulator Use](https://bitrig.com/blog/bitrig-simulator-use) , and you can[select an element](https://bitrig.com/blog/select-to-edit-in-the-simulator) on the CarPlay screen to show it exactly what to change.


-


**Request the entitlement.** Bitrig walks you through requesting Apple’s[CarPlay entitlement](https://developer.apple.com/contact/request/carplay/) : accept the agreement, pick your app’s category, and submit. My audio app was approved the same day.


-


**Use it in your car.** Run your app on your iPhone with one click and connect it to your car. When it’s ready to share,[Bitrig can publish it to the App Store](https://bitrig.com/blog/bitrig-publishes-to-the-app-store) .


You can do all of this from[Bitrig Remote](https://bitrig.com/remote) too. Prompt the agent, test your app in the CarPlay simulator, and[install it on your Home Screen](https://bitrig.com/blog/bitrig-remote-install-and-distribute-apps) with one tap, so it’s ready the next time you get in the car.


Your audio and video CarPlay apps will also work on[Apple HomeView](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/10/meet-apple-homeview-a-new-way-to-enjoy-entertainment-and-manage-the-home/) when it arrives on November 13.


So if you’ve had an idea for a CarPlay app, stop procrastinating. Bitrig makes it easy.
